title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (p.d.) de Rham complex. The aim is an integral, or arbitrary-ring, analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms.

Setup. For a ring h and each n, let L_n be the free h-module on the barycentric coordinates t_0,...,t_n and Φ_n = dL_n. Put
  D_n = Γ*(L_n) ⊗ Λ(Φ_n),
the p.d. de Rham complex of the affine cone A^{n+1} over the simplex. It is bigraded by D^{p,q}, with p the polynomial/weight degree and q the form degree. It is functorial in [n], so D_* is a simplicial bigraded commutative dg-algebra.

Key fact (marginal note 'homogène' alg. diff. = résolution de h). Over any h the p.d. de Rham complex of affine space is exact in positive weight. This is the divided-power Poincaré lemma, Koszul-dual to the exactness of Sym ⊗ Λ. So D_n is a resolution of h.

The simplex forms. Let T = Σ t_i ∈ D^{1,0}. The (homogeneous) p.d. forms on the simplex are
  C_* = D_*/(dT),
the quotient by the ideal generated by dT. The relation T = 1 is not imposed; the bigrading replaces dehomogenization, which is the natural choice since T^{[n]} cannot be dehomogenized integrally.

Kernel description. dT is part of a basis of the free module Φ_n, so the Koszul complex (Λ Φ, dT∧) is exact. Hence
  Λ^q/(dT∧Λ^{q-1}) ≅ dT∧Λ^q = Ker(dT∧ : Λ^{q+1} → Λ^{q+2}).
This gives C^{p,q}_* ≅ Ker(D^{p,q+1}_* → D^{p,q+2}_*), the map being multiplication by dT.

Passing to a simplicial set. For a simplicial set X_*, set C(X_*,h) = Hom(X_*, C_*) and D(X_*,h) = Hom(X_*, D_*). Hom(X_*, -) is left exact, so the kernel description passes to X_*:
  C^{p,q}_DRpd(X_*,h) ≅ Ker(D^{p,q+1}(X_*,h) → D^{p,q+2}(X_*,h)).
The expression of C as a cokernel would not pass to X_*.

Programme. All structures on C(X_*,h) (products, p.d. operations, ...) should be read off from 'structures to be made explicit' on D(X_*,h). D comes from the linear cone over the simplices; this is presumably what the opening sentence means by a 'linear' invariant finer a priori than C_DRpd. Grothendieck proposes to define 'the homotopical p.d. multiplicative structure of the homotopy type X_*', from which C_DRpd(X_*,h) can be recovered up to isomorphism via D(X_*,h), or via De Rham–Sullivan complexes.

Continuation on the next page. He does not know whether the p.d. de Rham complex (better: D(X_*,Z)) recovers the full unipotent p.d. cohomological structure, under finiteness conditions. If it does not, that finer 'linear' complex, in a suitable derived category, would be the 'motivic' candidate for the homotopy type of a connected, simply connected X_*.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. The isomorphism coker(dT) ≅ ker(dT on the next degree) needs exactness of the Koszul complex of dT in ΛΦ. This holds because dT = Σ dt_i is unimodular (a basis element after change of basis); Grothendieck does not state it but it is true.

The isomorphism C(X_*,h) ≅ Ker(D(X_*,h) → D(X_*,h)) is correctly stated in its kernel form. The cokernel form would not commute with Hom(X_*, -), and Grothendieck switches to the kernel form, presumably for this reason.
Whether the simplicial objects C_* and D_* are 'contractible'/extendable (the analogue of Sullivan's extendability needed for a de Rham theorem) is not addressed on this page.

ideas.what: Simplicial divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices, C_DRpd, as an integral analogue of Sullivan's forms.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cenkl–Porter (polynomial forms over Z, early 1980s); divided-power ideas go back to H. Cartan's 1954–55 seminar
ideas.where_published: Only in these 1976 IHES lecture notes (unpublished), to my knowledge

ideas.what: Realize simplex forms as the quotient of the acyclic homogeneous p.d. de Rham complex of the affine cone A^{n+1} by dT (T = Σ t_i), with the bigrading replacing the relation T = 1. Equivalently, describe them as Ker(dT·) one degree up, so that they pass to simplicial sets by left exactness.
ideas.modern_name: homogeneous (cone) model of simplex forms; Koszul complex of dT

ideas.what: Derive all algebraic structure on the forms of X_* from the finer simplicial 'linear' object D(X_*,h) of cone forms.
ideas.modern_name: a refined algebraic model of cochains (compare E∞/binomial models)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; nearest modern analogues are Mandell (E∞ cochains) and Toën/Horel (binomial/affine stacks)

ideas.what: Ask whether the p.d. de Rham complex (or D(X,Z)) determines the unipotent p.d. homotopy type integrally; if not, propose D as the 'motivic' model of simply connected homotopy types in a derived category.
ideas.modern_name: integral algebraic models of homotopy types / Grothendieck's schematization problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, 1983, schematization); Toën (affine stacks 2006, 'schématisation revisité' 2020); Mandell (2006); Horel (2022)
ideas.where_published: Schematization appears in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and the letter to Breen. The 1976 p.d. de Rham version seems unpublished.

missed.claim: In 1976 Grothendieck proposed an integral 'motivic' model of simply connected homotopy types. It is built from a divided-power de Rham complex of the cones over simplices, D(X_*,Z), and is meant to be finer than the p.d. simplex forms. This predates by seven years the schematization programme of Pursuing Stacks and is a p.d./de Rham precursor of it. The question whether p.d. forms recover the full unipotent p.d. homotopy type was left open.
missed.quote: On peut aussi définir "La structure multiplicative à p.d. homotopique du type d'homotopie X_*" ... qui permet de reconstituer ... C_DRpd(X_*,h), par D(X_*,h)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Current work on integral models (Mandell's E∞ cochains, Toën's affine stacks, Horel's and Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov's derived binomial rings) could be compared with an explicit commutative divided-power dg model built from cone forms. Asking whether the 'homogeneous' D-model carries strictly more information than C is a concrete, testable question.

missed.claim: This page links divided-power de Rham theory (the crystalline side) directly to rational/integral homotopy theory (Sullivan), as a 'motivic' homotopy type. The 1976 date predates the comparable literature (Cenkl–Porter, Mandell, Toën) known to me.
missed.quote: ce serait cette dernière cplx. "linéaire" qui serait le candidat motivique pour exprimer le type d'homotopie (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical priority point for the schematization problem's genesis, and a possible alternative (p.d.-algebra rather than binomial-ring) route to integral homotopy models.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra on the page (the cone resolution, the Koszul trick for dT, left exactness) is routine. Historically notable is the 1976 formulation of an integral divided-power 'motivic' model of simply connected homotopy types, earlier than Pursuing Stacks. That said, divided-power polynomial forms were studied by Cenkl–Porter, and the schematization idea itself is known and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'i.e. dis. qui est une résolution de h': the image reads roughly 'i.e. disons qui est une résolution de h' ('visolution' is 'résolution').
'structure multiplicative à h homotopique' is very likely 'à p.d. homotopique' (structure with divided powers).

The opening lines are partly illegible. They likely say one can associate to a topological space (or simplicial set) X_* an invariant in 'linear' algebras finer a priori than C_DRpd; 'dans l'ensemble des alg.' is uncertain.
In the kernel formula, the label under the arrow reads 'produit par dT'.
